response: The clustering has improved but still has significant mixing issues. The "Exoplanet Formation and Characterization" cluster contains neutron star mass/radius measurements, planetary nebulae, and solar system body papers that don't belong together — neutron star papers should go to high-energy astrophysics, and solar system/icy moon papers to planetary astrophysics. The "Black Holes and Galaxies" cluster is conflating galactic/extragalactic topics (galaxy simulations, barred galaxies) with high-energy phenomena (supernovae, neutron star binaries) — these should be split so that galaxy structure and stellar populations form a dedicated galactic/extragalactic cluster, while compact object and explosive transient papers join high-energy astrophysics. There is also no dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster yet; papers on stellar atmospheres, stellar evolution, and solar physics are likely scattered across other clusters and should be consolidated into one.
